clue.text: What flypaper might do for its potential victim

definitions.text: What flypaper might do for its potential victim

parts.words: What flypaper might do for its potential victim
parts.note: read literally, flypaper glues fast the little creature that lands on it: a verb plus its object, which also names a twig-like creature

explanation.surface: A musing on the fate awaiting a fly that blunders onto sticky paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase, the answer is an instruction: flypaper will stick (fasten) an insect. Read as a name, it is the twig-mimicking creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase doubles as the name of a slender creature resembling a twig, kept as a classroom pet.

clue.text: Noted changes getting firm through exercise

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the word noted are rearranged

explanation.surface: Observing that one's body is getting harder from working out.
explanation.definitionFit: Toned muscles are firm and defined from regular training.

clue.text: Way of paying chemical company pound supplement

parts.note: COD is cash on delivery, a method of payment
ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a British firm
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A firm's pound-based top-up to its payment terms.
explanation.walkthrough: ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was once Britain's biggest chemical maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A codicil is a supplement added to a will.

clue.text: Minor key adopted by popular worker

indicators.note: something adopted is taken in, so one piece goes inside the others

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
an ant is the classic worker in crosswords
F is a musical key

explanation.surface: A young child in a minor key taken in by a well-liked labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor' looks like the musical scale beside 'key', but it is the definition: a child under the age of legal adulthood.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor is someone legally a child, like an infant in law.

clue.text: Joint that ought to be put in front of the Queen

indicators.text: to be put in front of
indicators.note: this piece stands before the royal letters in the answer

parts.note: ought to means should
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Something deemed worth presenting before the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The shoulder is the joint linking arm to body.

clue.text: Took a risk — most of area by altar beginning to deteriorate

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the chancel is the part of a church around the altar

indicators.note: beginning means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Gambling that most of a church's sanctuary will start to crumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims CHANCEL to CHANCE; 'beginning to' gives D.
explanation.definitionFit: To chance it is to take a gamble.

clue.text: Firm, being calm, produced somewhere for the kids to play

definitions.text: somewhere for the kids to play

indicators.note: produced means made into something new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A steady company manufacturing playground equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing frame is a playground structure children clamber on.

clue.text: In no way corrupt, thus replacing America's expert

indicators.note: replacing means one piece takes the place of another

parts.note: virtuous means morally upright, not corrupt
US is the United States, America
so means thus

explanation.surface: An honest American specialist put in place of another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' swaps the US in VIRTUOUS for SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso is an expert performer, especially in music.

clue.text: Timed trainees changing racing tyres

indicators.note: changing means altering the order of the letters

explanation.surface: Learner drivers on a clock swapping the tyres on their racing cars.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing, intermediates are tyres for damp conditions, between slicks and wets.

clue.text: Curtains might be creased

definitions.meaning: curtains are often given a backing layer of fabric
creased in the sense of wrinkled, marked with furrows

explanation.definitionFit: Curtains with a backing fabric are described this way, and a creased face is one marked with furrows.

clue.text: Company share issue may be not a lot if worked out

indicators.note: working something out reorganises it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark that a firm's stock market debut will raise little once calculated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' rearranges NOT A LOT IF; 'if' reads as part of the condition but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating a company means offering its shares on the stock market for the first time.

clue.text: Italian family sourcing nuts and leaves of health-giving properties

parts.note: the Medici were the ruling banking family of Renaissance Florence

indicators.note: the source of each word is where it starts, so take the first letters

explanation.surface: Renaissance Florentines gathering nuts and leaves for herbal remedies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sourcing' takes the initial letters N, A, L of 'nuts and leaves'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with healing properties is curative, the adjective for remedies.

clue.text: Ignore! That's a smart girl

parts.note: to cut someone is to snub or ignore them
i.e. (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: Someone dismissing a remark as simply a clever young woman's.
explanation.definitionFit: A cute girl is attractive and sharp, the slang term for a pretty, clever young woman.

clue.text: Run through a white man's self-description

definitions.meaning: to pierce with a sword or spike
a pale-skinned man might say of himself '...', which runs together into the answer

explanation.definitionFit: To pierce a body with a blade or stake is to skewer it, and the phrase I'M PALE describes a white man.

clue.text: Bird finding hotel for student in Nice

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: nice means pleasant
L is a learner, a student
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Spotting a bird at a hotel standing in for a student in the French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the French city but means pleasant; 'for' puts H in place of L.
explanation.definitionFit: The pheasant is a long-tailed game bird.

clue.text: Fell back after principal gets clearance

indicators.note: the reversed fell comes after the principal in the answer

parts.note: the head is the principal of a school

indicators.note: going back means the word for fell is read in reverse

parts.note: a fell is a moor, upland in northern England

explanation.surface: A headteacher being given permission after a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns MOOR to ROOM. 'Fell' looks like a verb but is the northern English word for moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: Headroom is the clearance above one's head, as under a bridge or in a car.

clue.text: Birds looking embarrassed on sides of stage?

parts.note: red means blushing, embarrassed
the wings are the areas at the sides of a stage

explanation.surface: Performers blushing as they wait offstage.
explanation.definitionFit: Redwings are thrushes that winter in Britain.

clue.text: Teenager getting drunk on this? No

definitions.text: Teenager getting drunk on this? No

indicators.note: someone drunk is mixed up, so the letters of the word teenager are scrambled

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a youth could become intoxicated on a mild beverage, and concluding not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting drunk' rearranges TEENAGER; the whole clue also defines: no teenager gets drunk on this Chinese brew.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfermented tea leaves make a drink with no alcohol, so nobody gets drunk on it.

clue.text: More unpleasant sort of retsina

indicators.note: sort of means a version of, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumble about a particularly bad brand of Greek wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges RETSINA, a resin-flavoured Greek wine.

clue.text: Supply a source of fuel to cross river

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, its first letter

parts.note: to ford is to cross a river at a shallow place

clue.text: Region finding a way to support cost of travel?

parts.note: a fare is the price of a journey

clue.text: Go hungry, needing to look about five!

parts.note: to stare is to look fixedly
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A child left without food, looking about five years old.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve is to suffer from lack of food.

clue.text: Got up and started smelling the flowers

parts.note: rose, past tense of rise, means got up

indicators.note: started means only the opening letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Waking and beginning the day by smelling the blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose is a classic garden bloom, so the plural names flowers.

clue.text: Later, a few cooked crustacean

explanation.surface: A promise to prepare some shellfish later.
explanation.definitionFit: The daphnia, a tiny pond creature, is a freshwater crustacean.

clue.text: No-hoper is nearer being executed

indicators.note: an executed person is beheaded, so the first letter goes

parts.note: closer means nearer

clue.text: My French Italian gentleman's address in the Vatican

signor is the Italian title for a man, like Mr

explanation.surface: Musing on how one's Italian friend is addressed in Rome's papal city.
explanation.definitionFit: Monsignor is the title used to address certain senior Catholic prelates.

clue.text: Man for example after a passage

indicators.note: the island comes after the article in the answer

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A fellow following someone through a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person but is the Isle of Man, an island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passageway between rows of seats.

clue.text: Searchers whose views include people from the ranks

indicators.note: include means one part is placed within the other

parts.note: prospects are views or outlooks
